records.Concise description: A 100-piece very-early Ordinals rock collection commonly associated with the pseudonymous creator rocktoshi / Ordrocks.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Rocks is an early 100-work Ordinals collection whose appeal centers on extreme inscription provenance and a deliberately simple rock aesthetic. The name has been reused by unrelated later projects, making source hygiene important. MSC should tie the canonical profile to the early Ordrocks/rocktoshi lineage rather than any newer same-name collection.
records.Launch / history: Inscribed during the very early 2023 Ordinals period; the earliest works are commonly placed near the first ~100 inscriptions.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: Along with Ordinal Punks and other sub-1k works, Bitcoin Rocks helped establish extreme early inscription provenance as a collector category.
records.Verification basis: Multiple Ordinals index/market sources; standalone early project source requires archival confirmation.
Research notes / uncertainties: Several unrelated sites/projects use 'Bitcoin Rocks'; do not link a newer project as the canonical early collection.
Exact earliest inscription number and creator handle should be archival-verified before public numerical copy.

records.Concise description: Yuga Labs’ 300-piece generative Ordinals art project organized around a 12×12 grid and base-12 visual system.
records.Deeper researched summary: TwelveFold was Yuga Labs’ standalone Bitcoin art experiment. Official launch material described 300 generative works, with 288 sold by auction and 12 reserved for contributors/philanthropic/other project purposes. Yuga explicitly positioned it as separate from its Ethereum collections and without a broader roadmap. The finite project is therefore classified historical/completed.
records.Launch / history: Announced and auctioned in February–March 2023. 288 of 300 pieces were offered in the initial auction; 12 were reserved.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It was an early, high-profile commitment to Ordinals from one of the largest existing NFT studios and helped validate Bitcoin inscriptions as a serious generative-art medium.
records.Verification basis: Yuga Labs first-party launch material and TwelveFold site.
Research notes / uncertainties: Treat as completed/historical; do not infer active roadmap from Yuga’s continued corporate activity.

records.Concise description: A 21,000-piece Ordinals distribution experiment that gamified a pre-Runes 'mining' phase and later connected holders to RSIC•GENESIS•RUNE.
records.Deeper researched summary: RSIC distributed 21,000 rune-like inscriptions to selected Ordinals wallets in January 2024 and used an off-chain/indexer/game layer to accumulate points or 'runes' before the actual Runes protocol launched. After the 2024 halving, the project’s continuation moved into the Runes ecosystem through RSIC•GENESIS•RUNE. The Ordinals phase is a completed historical experiment; the related Rune belongs canonically in RUNES.
Creators / founders: RSIC project team — individual founder attribution not sufficiently first-party verified
records.Launch / history: 21,000 RSIC inscriptions distributed in January 2024 ahead of the Runes protocol activation at the 2024 halving; later transitioned into a Rune-linked phase.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: RSIC was an influential pre-Runes experiment showing how inscriptions could bootstrap distribution, game mechanics, and community before a fungible-asset protocol went live.
records.Verification basis: On-chain/indexer records and current market history; project-controlled archival source not fully locked.
Research notes / uncertainties: The pre-Runes accumulation system was not Bitcoin mining and must not be described as protocol-level proof-of-work.
Canonical Rune profile belongs in RUNES.

records.Concise description: A small early Ordinals Pepe collection whose works were inscribed around the low-thousands and deliberately referenced the older Rare Pepes/Bitcoin meme lineage.
records.Deeper researched summary: Inscribed Pepes brought Pepe imagery into the early inscription era and is typically indexed as a 69-piece collection around inscriptions #2,115–#2,189. Its historical significance comes less from later roadmap activity than from connecting Ordinals to the much older Bitcoin Counterparty/Rare Pepe culture. Creator attribution remains insufficiently verified.
Creators / founders: Creator/founding attribution unresolved in the current research pass
records.Launch / history: Inscribed during the early 2023 Ordinals period, around the low-thousands inscription range.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It links Ordinals meme culture directly to the Rare Pepe tradition that predated Ordinals by years.
Research notes / uncertainties: Rare Pepes are pre-Ordinals Counterparty assets and should be related history, not duplicated as Ordinals entities.
